title: Data Scientist
reason: Stack +38; Synergy +10; Title fit +6; US +10
description_preview:
Who We Are
Melotech is revolutionizing media and entertainment. We create art through technology for humans to enjoy. In just 24 months, our work has been heard, watched and loved for over 4 billion minutes worldwide.
Founded by entrepreneur and investor Soheil Mirpour, we are backed by top VCs Cherry Ventures, Speedinvest and GFC, alongside world-class angels from firms such as Spotify, Blackstone and KKR.
What You Will Do
Join us as our first dedicated Data Scientist to bring order to the chaos of culture. You'll extract insights from hard-to-reach data sources to tackle the big questions: What cultural trends are emerging that everyone else is missing? How can we predict virality? And what characterizes an underserved category? We sit on a lot of data we do not use yet, and you are the person who turns it into decisions. You work fully autonomously alongside our founder and the team, next to a backend engineer who owns the pipelines and infrastructure, so your time goes into the questions rather than the plumbing. On a typical day, your tasks may include:
New data sources: discovering and opening up untapped sources, with creative scraping and acquisition techniques when standard APIs run out
Trends and audiences: analyzing trends, audience behavior and performance across streaming and social to find the underserved categories and the next growth opportunity, and proposing the next step
Prediction: prototyping and deploying ML models on AWS for virality prediction and content analysis, and checking whether they hold up in production
Experiments: designing and reading A/B tests, holdouts and spend experiments across our releases and campaigns, and telling the team where the next dollar should go
Numbers people trust: owning the dashboards and reports leadership runs on, and investigating what really drives a metric when it moves
AI-native workflows: using LLMs and agentic coding tools to accelerate data cleaning, analysis and reporting
Who You Are
We look for battle-tested data scientists who understand that real impact comes from turning messy, unstructured data into business-critical insights that drive company direction. You don't just build models: you solve business problems by finding creative ways to access hard-to-reach data and translating statistical findings into actions the team takes.
Typically, Your Profile Will Look Like This
Background: a degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Math or a related quantitative field
Experience: 3 or more years of hands-on data science in fast-paced business environments, at Tier 1 consultancies, Big Tech, high-growth start-ups and scale-ups, or media industry leaders
Python: expert-level proficiency with the standard data science and ML frameworks, and SQL as a daily tool
Data acquisition: you have scraped and acquired raw data from new sources, building creative solutions to reach datasets beyond standard APIs
Statistical rigour: you design and read experiments properly, you know when a signal is noise, and you have run A/B tests or causal analyses that changed a decision
Models in production: you have deployed models that people actually used, and you know what it takes to keep them honest over time
AI-native: extensive hands-on experience with agentic coding tools and LLMs in your data workflows
From data to decision: you find the opportunity in the data and propose the next step, and your dashboards and visualizations (standard libraries or Tableau) are the ones leadership trusts
Collaboration: you work well across engineering, product and business teams, and colleagues would describe you as hard-working, ambitious and persistent
Pace: you thrive in a fast-paced and performance-oriented environment
A big plus: you're obsessed with music, video or social media
What Makes This Exciting
You are one of the first employees of an ambitious team, changing the world of media and entertainment. Being early means every decision you make shapes our trajectory. You're not a cog in the machine but the captain of your own ship, rewarded for performance and respected for leadership. Flat hierarchies mean that your voice matters, your ideas get implemented, and your impact is immediate.
We pay competitive salaries and make you an owner of the business with equity. We work remotely to give you complete freedom over your life, while meeting regularly around the world for global offsites where we strategize, bond, and push boundaries together.
What The Process Will Look Like
We hire on a rolling basis. Earliest starting date is always ASAP.
Once You Begin Our Process, You Can Progress From Start To Offer Within a Week, Depending On How Quickly You Can Move Through Each Stage
Initial interview: 30-minute introductory call, getting to know you
Case interview: 90-minute case discussion, present and debate your skills
Founder interview: 90-minute interview with our CEO, going deep on all topics
Offer, contract signing and onboarding
Note: As we are still in stealth, you will learn more about Melotech as you progress through the stages. By the end of the Founder interview, you will have a full grasp of our business and the details of your role.

description_preview:
San Francisco, CA
In Person
Full-Time
Applying to this role will also allow us to consider you for other research opportunities at Vizcom. We believe the best roles are shaped around exceptional people, not just job descriptions.
About Vizcom
Vizcom is where design teams at companies like Nike, GM, New Balance, and Hasbro bring ideas from sketch to product. Designers use Vizcom to sketch, render, explore color and materials, work in 3D, and prepare concepts for production.
The render itself was never the point. The point is the physical thing that comes after it. We call this
pencil to product
.
Vizcom is a Series B company with more than $52M raised.
More than 700,000 designers have worked in Vizcom, and every session leaves a trail: candidates selected, outputs promoted into designs, regions masked and renamed, and entire directions kept or discarded.
That trail is one of the most valuable things we create outside of the product itself. Today, though, it's more archaeology than asset. Only a fraction of what happens in a session reaches training-grade quality, while increasingly sophisticated post-training methods depend on exactly this kind of high-quality, domain-specific data.
Your job will be to help turn that trail into a machine.
A design session isn't a simple sequence — it's a branching tree. Designers fork, backtrack, iterate, and abandon entire directions on their way to the thing they ultimately keep. The judgment lives in the shape of that process, and today we capture only pieces of it.
The Role
As an
ML Data Engineer
, you'll build and improve the systems that turn professional design work into training-grade preference data and training results back into a better product.
You'll work alongside the researchers consuming what you build, within the product systems where these signals originate, and across the data infrastructure where they ultimately land. Your closest users are the researchers sitting beside you, and you'll see quickly when a dataset you've built allows them to ask a question they couldn't ask before.
This is not a support role, and it isn't traditional offline ETL.
The pipelines you work on will run through a live product used every day by professional design teams, including enterprise customers with rigorous expectations around privacy and data protection. Capturing better signals without compromising user trust, contractual obligations, or product performance is a core part of the work.

About Geek+
Geek+ is a robotics and AI company specializing in AI-powered logistics solutions. Founded in Beijing in 2015, we have grown into the largest independent logistics robotics company in the world, with operations across the globe. Our North American headquarters in San Diego, California, and our innovation center in Suwanee, Georgia, drive our continued growth in the United States, Canada, and LatAm.
We're now building our first North American manufacturing facility in Atlanta, and we're looking for an Associate Manufacturing Engineer to help bring robot production online.
Life at Geek+
Plain and simple: we're a team of geeks who love technology and teamwork. We work together to meet any customer need, we celebrate our wins, and we learn from our misses. The only thing better than seeing a customer's operations improved by our technology is seeing it happen at scale. About Skan
Skan automates automation. We capture how work actually happens across an organization and autonomously turn that observation into automation. We are now building toward agentic automation of that work: systems that operate over observed process data and generate Agentic Operating Procedures, structured and auditable playbooks mined from direct observation that allow agents to understand the steps, decisions, branches, and exceptions that define how work is actually performed.
We are a small and passionate team of researchers, engineers, and domain experts working on the next generation of agentic automation: self-discovered AI agents that can understand and operate real enterprise software.
About The Role
Before an agent can reliably operate software on a user's behalf, it needs to understand what should happen next and why: the underlying process, its steps, decision points and governing logic, branches, variations, dependencies, and long-tail edge cases. In practice, this knowledge is rarely represented explicitly. It is distributed across messy event logs, unstructured documents, screen recordings, UI interaction traces, historical executions, and the tacit knowledge of domain experts.
As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will work across teams to develop process-agnostic, scalable learning systems that recover the latent structure, decision logic, and dynamics underlying complex process execution trajectories from sparse, noisy, highly correlated observations spanning substantial behavioral heterogeneity and organizational scale.
You will take heterogeneous data such as action logs, noisy screen traces, semi-structured documents, and variant-heavy workflows, and build systems that recover canonical process structure, meaningful variations, decision rules, dependencies, exceptions, and provenance. These representations are consumed by downstream agentic execution systems and must preserve enough detail for an agent to act correctly while remaining structured, compact, transparent, and auditable.
The same observational data and learned representations also contribute directly to our work on computer-use models for last-mile interaction with enterprise software.
The problems here rarely arrive with clean formulations. You may begin with a branch the system consistently fails to recover, two superficially different execution paths that should collapse into the same process, or an algorithm that works across thousands of traces but fails at millions. Your job is to turn those failures into tractable research problems: identify the right abstraction, formulate hypotheses, design evaluations that isolate the problem, and develop methods that solve it. Depending on the problem, this may draw from process and decision mining, graph algorithms, structured prediction, representation learning, information retrieval, program synthesis, model post-training and distillation, or agentic systems.
We care less about allegiance to a particular technique than about finding the simplest method that reliably recovers the underlying structure and scales.
Responsibilities
Process discovery and representation: Build pipelines that discover, extract, and formalize end-to-end business processes from event logs, UI interaction traces, screen recordings, and unstructured documents.
Develop algorithms for process variant detection, noise removal, and trace consolidation, turning noisy, high-cardinality action sequences into clean canonical representations.
Design representations that preserve the information downstream agents need while collapsing irrelevant execution-level variation.
Study the tradeoff between abstraction and fidelity: determine when superficially different trajectories represent the same underlying behavior and when small differences encode materially different decisions.
Build retrieval and grounding systems that incorporate SOPs, documents, and domain knowledge when process understanding requires evidence beyond execution traces.
Evaluation and reliability: Develop rigorous evaluation frameworks for process discovery and extraction, including LLM-as-Judge pipelines, conformance checking against ground-truth processes, and regression suites that catch subtle degradation.
Develop evaluation methods for settings where there may not be a single canonical ground truth, including behaviorally equivalent process representations.
Enumerate and systematically test exception paths, conditional branches, loops, rare variants, and the failure modes that naive extraction approaches miss.
Make deliberate algorithmic tradeoffs so systems remain tractable across millions of traces and thousands of variants, including choices around data structures, approximation, indexing, and level of abstraction.
Diagnose failures in production and turn recurring failure patterns into new algorithmic or research directions.
Collaboration: Work closely with the computer-use agents team so the representations you produce are expressed at the right level of abstraction, contain the necessary execution context, and are robust enough for downstream autonomous execution.
Work across research, engineering, and product to move promising methods from prototype to production and measure their effect on downstream agent behavior.

We’re SmartThings, one of the leading IoT ecosystems in the world, creating the most effortless way for anyone to create a smart home. We're a wholly owned subsidiary of Samsung with corporate offices in Minneapolis and the Bay Area.
More than 430 million people worldwide use SmartThings to control and manage their connected life. SmartThings delivers simple, powerful experiences across Samsung’s leading portfolio of phones, TVs, and appliances. We also offer the most versatile smart home experience as an open platform with a rich partner ecosystem (think IKEA, SONOS, Honeywell, and so many more). As a founding member of Matter, we are a leader in the industry to help make smart homes more secure, reliable and seamless to use. Come be a part of the leading edge of IoT innovation!
We are looking for a
Full Stack Software Engineer
to join our Developer Center team. Device makers around the world integrate their hardware with the SmartThings platform, and the Developer Center is where that journey happens, from first API call through Works with SmartThings certification. It's how developers around the world experience our platform, and our team's mission is to make that journey clear, accurate, and easy to use.
This role owns the documentation developers rely on and helps build the console they use alongside it. You'll write the integration guides and API reference at developer.smartthings.com/docs, own that site's frontend and publishing pipeline, and contribute features and code to the Developer Center itself. You'll collaborate across product and engineering teams to deliver a seamless, high-quality developer experience for the global SmartThings platform.
Key Responsibilities
This position is a hybrid role, based onsite 3 days a week at our office in Minneapolis, MN.
In this role, your primary responsibilities will include the following:
Own the docs site on the SmartThings Developer Center end to end: Docusaurus theme customization, MDX components, versioning, search configuration, CI/CD, and analytics.
Write and maintain technical documentation (API docs, SDK guides, and integration tutorials) for external developers integrating with the SmartThings platform.
Establish documentation standards, and maintain quality through linters, AI-powered authoring tools, and participation in code and documentation reviews.
Collaborate cross-functionally with platform engineers, product managers, and designers to build new features and enhance existing ones for the Developer Center.
Use AI tooling to accelerate drafting, research, and content audits, with technical verification before anything ships.
Proactively communicate progress and challenges to stakeholders and team.
Skills, Knowledge & Expertise
Inclusive Hiring Practices
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At SmartThings, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
What You Bring On Day One (Required Qualifications)
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or related field
2+ years combined across software engineering and technical writing.
Demonstrated strong technical writing for a developer audience.
Experience with Docusaurus or comparable documentation frameworks.
Strong proficiency with HTML, CSS/SCSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, and React.
Experience with Node.js and frameworks such as Express or Next.js
Comfortable owning a build and deploy pipeline: CI/CD, previews, static site builds.
Strong information architecture instincts: can take a sprawling topic and give it a structure a stranger can navigate.

Familiarity with Java or Kotlin.
Self-motivated with a strong intellectual curiosity.
Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning, with the ability to quickly acquire and apply new skills in a fast-evolving environment.

A collaborative mindset, actively sharing knowledge to elevate the skills and performance of the broader team.
Experience building with AI and authoring content consumed by AI agents.
Experience with SEO, generative engine optimization (GEO), web accessibility (WCAG), and Google Analytics.
SmartThings Benefits

Job Title: Salesforce - Developer
You are a Salesforce Developer with experience solving complex problems on the Salesforce platform. As a Salesforce developer you have knowledge of the technical domains of Salesforce including the various cloud platforms, programmatic development, declarative solutioning and integrations. Execute test plans to ensure quality delivery

Absorb new product and technical capabilities from Salesforce during new product releases and acquisitions

Proven ability to develop andoptimizeintegrated business processes across disparate systems
Understanding of the Salesforce platform including Sales Cloud, Service Cloud,ExperienceCloudand common AppExchange solutions

Experience with Salesforce APIs (REST/SOAP/Metadata, etc.)
Front-end development experience with Lightning Web Components
Knowledge of integrations, 3rd party integration tools, ETL with Salesforce
Knowledge of Object-Oriented Analysis and Design, databasedesignand software development lifecycle
Experience in Agile Methodology
Experience and exposure in Einstein and Salesforce AI product capabilities
Experience in CI/CD Salesforce services and processes
Problem-solving skills with the ability to work cross-functionally either on a team or as an individual contributor
Active Salesforce certifications or ability to achieve relevant certifications upon hire
Excellent client-facing written, presentation and verbal communications skills

Who We Are
SEI conducts research and development in software engineering, systems engineering, cybersecurity, and many other areas of computing, working to introduce private-sector innovations into government. The SEI works closely with defense and government organizations, industry, and academia to continually improve software-intensive systems. Its core purposes are to help organizations improve software engineering capabilities, advance cybersecurity methods and technologies, and bring the discipline of software engineering to AI systems.
What We Do
The CERT Threat Analysis (TA) Directorate conducts research and development activities to identify, analyze, coordinate disclosure, and mitigate threats and vulnerabilities in systems and software. The TA Directorate is currently comprised of three teams: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Security, Malware and Vulnerability Exploitation, and Platform and Mission Engineering. The AI Security team works on advancing the state of the art in AI security at a national and global scale. The Malware and Vulnerability Exploitation (MVE) team works to improve cyber-tradecraft analysis within strategic target communities to counter adversarial use of the Internet and related technologies. The vulnerability side of MVE (home of the CERT Coordination Center) works with an expansive network of vendors, partners, and collaborators to reduce the societal harm of vulnerable software and systems. The Platform and Mission Engineering team develops and maintains tools, environments, and operational support for the malware analysis, reverse engineering, vulnerability analysis, and AI security domains.
Position Summary
As an AI Red Team Engineer on the AI Security team, you will play a central role in adversary emulation exercises and capability development for our mission partners. Due to our unique position within the TA Directorate, the systems we red-team fall outside the realm of 'traditional' enterprise red teaming. Our targets are commonly AI-enabled platforms used within national security contexts.
But this isn't a "make the LLM say the bad thing" type of AI red team. We operate across multiple domains, meaning that our red teamers are expected to be experts in offensive cyber in addition to AI security. If you are experienced with offensive cyber tradecraft and have an interest in breaking into AI, this could be a good fit. Most of our red teamers are actively taking graduate-level technical courses at CMU and/or pursuing technical certifications. Perpetual learning is a core part of what we do.
While our red team exists within a research organization, research is only a portion of the work performed by our red team. Much of the work will involve red teaming real-world systems, sometimes at an aggressive cadence. This can involve planning and rehearsing red team TTPs, traveling to field sites, and presenting relevant findings. Like most red teams, we don't get to pick and choose our targets. This means that our red team needs to be well-rounded (both as individuals and as a team). Thus, we expect all applicants to be savvy with both Windows and Linux, solid with TCP/IP, and have some experience with penetration testing and/or red teaming (CTF experience may be relevant for Assistant and Associate levels).
What You’ll Do
Red team real-world AI-enabled systems (both the model and the hardware/software/network that it runs on) in support of national security objectives.
Develop new tactics, techniques, and procedures for attacking AI-enabled systems and related software in order to better prepare defenders for real-world threats.
Write tools in Python, PowerShell, C, and BASH to enable red team operations.
Represent the CERT technical portfolio of work and operations; communicate with external mission partners and internal collaborators in concert with CERT directorates and teams.
Who You Are
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or a relevant technical discipline with three (3) years of relevant work experience; or a MS in Computer Science or a relevant technical discipline with one (1) year of relevant work experience; or a PhD in Computer Science or other relevant technical discipline. Other educational backgrounds of a technical nature with experience as described may be considered.
You have previous penetration testing, red teaming, or exploit development experience.
You have previous hands-on experience with at least one command and control framework (e.g., Cobalt Strike, Sliver).
You have experience programming/scripting in Python, C, and BASH (without the assistance of AI) and are willing to learn PowerShell.
You have experience with reverse engineering tools (e.g. NSA Ghidra, IDA Pro).
You are able to read code and quickly spot basic vulnerabilities without the assistance of AI or fuzzing.
You are very familiar with TCP/IP and all layers of the OSI model. You have experience using Wireshark and can explain how common network protocols work.
You have experience in assessing the security of both Linux and Windows systems. Experience with mobile (e.g., Android) and other operations systems is also appreciated.
You have at least one of the following relevant certifications: OSCP, CPTS, FORGE/RIOT, eJPT, CBBH, BSCP, PNPT, GRTP, GPEN. Applicants without these certifications will still be considered if equivalent experience is clearly demonstrated during technical interviews.
You have excellent communication skills (oral and written), particularly regarding technical communications with non-experts.
You enjoy mentoring and cross-training others and sharing knowledge within the broader community.
You have a willingness to travel (25%) outside of your office location to other SEI offices, sponsor sites, conferences, and offsite meetings.
You will be subject to a background investigation, and you must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Department of War security clearance.

About Taxapp
TaxApp is a tax services company. Our main product, TaxApp, is the CRM our staff use to run tax cases and the portal our clients use to share information, sign forms and make payments. Our primary goal is to assist clients who owe backtaxes to the IRS and make the process simpler for them.
About the role
We're looking for a Support Engineer to be the first line of help when something in TaxApp isn't working. You'll work on site with the staff who use TaxApp every day and help our clients on the portal. When a problem comes in, you'll dig into the data, logs and code to explain exactly why it happened. Then you'll fix it yourself, whether it's a data issue, a configuration problem or a bug in the code, and make sure it stays fixed.
Your focus is keeping TaxApp working well rather than building new features. This role is for an experienced engineer who enjoys finding out why things break, fixing them properly, and explaining what happened calmly to the people affected.
You'll be joining a fast-paced, high-intensity environment, working closely with our sales, accounting and legal teams, who rely on TaxApp to serve clients. Priorities can shift quickly, especially during busy periods, so staying organized and calm under pressure matters.
We're also an AI-first team. Our senior engineers use AI coding tools to produce a large volume of code every day, so changes ship often. Be the first point of contact for TaxApp problems from two groups: staff in the CRM, such as case managers, office managers and team leads, and clients on the portal.

Mission Planning Autonomy Engineer (Simulation & Modeling) - Blue Ring
Job Description
As part of a hardworking team of engineers and mission operators within Blue Ring's Ground & Spaceflight Operations (GSO) organization, you will work closely with space vehicle, flight dynamics, and mission operations teams to develop, test, and deploy autonomy for the Mission Planning System (MPS), the cloud-native ground software that plans, schedules, validates, and dispatches activities across a fleet of Blue Ring spacecraft. MPS turns operator, customer, and flight dynamics requests into conflict-free, constraint-checked timelines, ground station contact plans, and onboard command sequences.
As a Mission Planning Autonomy Engineer, you will help move Blue Ring ground operations from human-in-the-loop toward human-on-the-loop. You will build the deterministic planning and scheduling engines, resource models, and simulation environments that let MPS generate, repair, and safely execute plans with progressively less operator intervention — and you will build the evidence that proves each step is safe. This role can be filled as an autonomy-focused software engineer or as a simulation and modeling engineer; both work on the same problem from different sides. Join us in enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth. Passion for our mission is required!
Special Mentions
Relocation provided

Design, implement, test, verify and deploy MPS planning and scheduling capabilities, including automated activity scheduling, deconfliction, replanning, and course-of-action generation across multiple spacecraft.
Build and evolve the MPS constraint engine and resource models (power, energy storage, onboard data volume, link budget, attitude keep-out, propellant/delta-V) used to validate plans before promotion and execution.
Develop the safety gates, runtime assurance checks, and fail-closed behaviors that govern when MPS may act automatically versus when an operator must approve or can veto.
Develop simulation and modeling capability for autonomy verification: spacecraft resource and behavior models, scenario generation, deterministic replay of recorded operations, Monte Carlo and stress campaigns, and shadow-mode comparison of automated plans against operator decisions.
Extend the spacecraft and ground station simulator to the fidelity needed to verify autonomy, and integrate it with the integration test framework and Software-in-the-Loop and Hardware-in-the-Loop environments.

You will join a multidisciplinary team supporting the build, operation and continuous improvement of enterprise Apigee environments. Support IBM API Connect and DataPower to Apigee migration waves through environment readiness, policy availability, routing, cutover, rollback validation, release support and hypercare.
Maintain platform documentation, deployment evidence, validation checklists, SOPs, runbooks, known-error articles and support transition materials.

You will succeed in this role by combining hands-on platform engineering with disciplined troubleshooting, automation and documentation. You should be comfortable working across development and operations teams, translating technical dependencies into practical actions, and maintaining quality during releases, incidents and migration activity.

A minimum of four years of relevant experience in Apigee platform administration, implementation, API gateway operations, DevOps or related platform engineering work.
Hands-on experience with Apigee proxies, shared flows, products, apps, environments, policies, analytics and management APIs.
Kubernetes operations experience covering pods, deployments, services, ingress, namespaces, secrets, config maps, RBAC, autoscaling, logging and troubleshooting.
Cloud platform exposure in GCP, AWS, Azure or hybrid/on-premises environments, including networking, IAM, load balancing, DNS and security fundamentals.
CI/CD implementation experience using tools such as Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Maven, shell scripting, Python or equivalent automation technologies.
Knowledge of API security, TLS/mTLS, certificates, OAuth2, JWT, API keys, rate limiting, quota, spike arrest and threat protection.
Experience with observability, production support, Linux, networking, YAML/JSON, Git, REST APIs, troubleshooting and technical documentation.
Ideally, you'll also have
Experience installing, upgrading or troubleshooting Apigee hybrid runtimes.
Exposure to Terraform, Helm, Kustomize, Ansible or GitOps for platform provisioning and configuration management.
Awareness of IBM API Connect or DataPower migration patterns, including API products, catalogs, policies, GatewayScript, XSLT and SOAP/XML.
Experience with DevSecOps or vulnerability scanning tools, regulated or multi-cloud environments, disaster recovery validation, capacity planning or platform resiliency testing.

title: AI Site Reliability Engineer
reason: Stack +49; Title fit +6; US +10; Senior desc -15; Overqualified -45; Senior salary -45
description_preview:
Cognizant is seeking an AI Site Reliability Engineer to build and operate the reliable, scalable, and secure infrastructure behind our AI and machine-learning platforms.
You will work across cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, GPU compute, model-serving systems, observability, automation, and incident response. You will partner with software, data science, security, and platform teams to ensure our AI systems meet high standards for availability, latency, performance, cost, and operational safety.
Responsibilities
Design, operate, and improve highly available infrastructure for AI training, inference, and data-processing workloads.
Define and manage service-level objectives, reliability metrics, error budgets, and capacity plans.
Build monitoring, logging, tracing, alerting, and AI-specific observability for model-serving platforms.
Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, post-incident reviews, and reliability improvements.
Automate deployment, scaling, rollback, disaster recovery, and routine operational tasks.
Operate Kubernetes-based services, cloud platforms, GPU clusters, networking, storage, and CI/CD systems.
Improve model-serving performance, including latency, throughput, GPU utilization, availability, and cost efficiency.
Develop safe automation and self-healing workflows for common production issues.
Establish operational standards for model versioning, rollouts, canary releases, feature flags, and rollback procedures.
Collaborate with engineering and ML teams to make AI systems production-ready.
Maintain clear runbooks, architecture documentation, and operational procedures.
Participate in an on-call rotation and help build a sustainable, low-noise operational culture.
Required Qualifications
4+ years of experience in SRE, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, platform engineering, or production engineering.
Strong Linux, networking, cloud, and distributed-systems experience.
Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform.
Experience with at least one major cloud platform: AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
Proficiency in Python, Go, or another programming language used for automation and production systems.
Experience with observability platforms, metrics, logs, traces, and incident-management practices.
Experience operating production services with defined availability and performance targets.
Strong troubleshooting, communication, documentation, and systems-thinking skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience operating machine-learning or generative-AI workloads in production.
Familiarity with GPUs, CUDA, model-serving systems, vector databases, or high-performance computing.
Experience with tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Argo CD, Helm, or service meshes.
Knowledge of MLOps practices, model lifecycle management, and ML/data pipelines.
Experience with reliability testing, chaos engineering, load testing, or capacity modeling.
Understanding of AI security, data privacy, model-safety controls, and access management.
Success in This Role
Within the first year, you will help reduce critical incidents, improve detection and recovery times, increase platform availability, improve infrastructure utilization, and create repeatable operational standards for deploying and running AI systems at scale.
The salary range for this role is between $142,000 and $167,500 depending on skills and qualifications of the candidate. Applications will be accepted till 10/31/2026
